reasoning: Failure-driven edits (container clues, acronym/'Its <property>' clues, single clean answer, plain person names, echo guard, verbatim-hit audit, multi-definition clues) are all kept intact. None conflicts with the success edits. Three success edits are kept because failure edits do not cover them: tribute-act-to-original-creator, part-of-name clues, and the head-noun-in-quotes / descriptor-plus-quote clues. Four anchor collisions were resolved so each insertion point is used once and ordering is unambiguous. (1) The grammar-role success edit and the head-noun-in-quotes success edit both fit the quoted-word bullet, so I merged them there. The grammar-role text now says it is an explicit exception to the failure-driven echo guard, which sits earlier in Rule 2. (2) The tribute-act success edit shared the 'Honor qualifiers' anchor with the failure acronym edit, so I moved it to the 'One of these <role/title>' bullet. (3) The failure edits keep their original anchors. (4) Nothing touches the protected SLOW_UPDATE markers.

edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Container clues: (a) a clue that is just ONE place name ('Hamburg') asks for the country, or for the US state if it is an American place. (b) 'this state's / this country's <thing>' ('Divisions of this state's Sumter National Forest include Long Cane, Enoree & Tiger') asks for the state or country that CONTAINS the named thing. The names inside the clue (divisions, districts, rivers, cities) only locate it and are never the answer. Passages about hotels, forests, trains, weather or teams for the place are search hits. Look for the passage that says the place is 'in <State/Country>' and give that bare name ('South Carolina', 'Germany').

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content:
- Acronym / expansion clues ('X stands for these ...', 'short for ...', 'the initials mean ...', or a capitalized abbreviation plus 'this feature/term': 'If your TV has PIP, it has this feature'): the answer is the spelled-out expansion exactly as a passage or passage title prints it ('Digimon' = 'Digital Monsters'; PIP = 'Picture in Picture'). Search the passages for the expansion next to the acronym. Never repeat the clue's own descriptor ('strange creatures') and never use a loose phrase from one forum snippet.
- 'It/Its <defining property or formula>' with no 'this' ('Its area equals pi r (squared)', 'Its boiling point is 100 degrees'): the answer is the WHOLE thing that has the property ('Circle'), not a variable, part or measure named in the formula or its explanation (not 'radius', not 'pi'). Ask: what object is this formula the area of? Name that object.

edits.target: - Put only the bare answer in the answer tags. Do not write a sentence, restate the clue, or add dates, qualifiers or alternatives. Brief reasoning belongs before the tags.
edits.content: - Commit to ONE answer. Never write 'X or Y' ('sheep or goat'). When passages list several animals, items or names, pick the one the passages stress most ('particularly sheep') and give it alone ('Sheep'). Copy the answer as clean text. Passages are often garbled by scraping, with stray letters glued to a word ('ragaE', 'pail and ragaE'). Strip such debris and give the normal word ('rag'). For a quoted line that ends before the missing word ('...to wash the steps with pail and' this), the answer is only the next word of the quotation.

edits.target: Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - Person names without a verbatim archive hit: give plain 'First Last' and drop a middle initial that appears only in formal passage text ('Lyndon Johnson', not 'Lyndon B. Johnson'; 'Harry Truman'). Keep an initial only when it is part of the universal form of the name, or when a verbatim archive line shows it. Never add titles such as 'President' or 'Sir' unless the archive line shows them.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - ECHO GUARD: after drafting an answer, compare it with the clue text. If your candidate (or a longer form of it) is a name, place or word the clue itself states, reject it: the clue names anchors, not the answer. 'In 1579 this English circumnavigator put the Golden Hind in for repairs at an inlet north of San Francisco' -> the circumnavigator (Drake), not 'San Francisco'. 'A "letter to" this person, like Ben Bradlee, ...' -> 'like X' gives an example of the role, so answer the role ('The editor'), not X. 'The university of this U.S. territory is home to the Micronesian Area Research Center' -> 'Guam', not 'University of Guam' (the pattern 'the <thing> of this <noun>' asks for the <noun> alone). 'The alliance of these Chinese businesses became a civil rights group' -> 'laundries', the plural members the pointer stands for, not the alliance's own name. A page or archive CATEGORY word ('SORRY YOU'RE POOR') is not the answer either. (The only exceptions are the grammar-role clues and the quoted generic head-noun clues described below.)

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - Verbatim-hit audit: before using your own knowledge, find any passage containing a long run of the clue's words and read what comes right after it: the text after '|' up to '. right:', or the last item after the final comma of an all-caps flashcard line ('...AN INLET NORTH OF SAN FRANCISCO, DRAKE.'). That text is the answer even if you 'know' a different one (clue 'organ meat, sometimes known as gossip's fate' + archive '| tongue. right: Leah.' -> 'tongue', not 'liver'). Never substitute a word from the clue when such a hit exists.

edits.target: A dictionary synonym that fits only one half ('trial') is wrong. When passages are noisy, use your own knowledge of sports terms and idioms.
edits.content: - Multi-definition and compound-word clues ('Aussie slang for a pub, it's also a shack; poor people may live in a "town" of them') join several senses with ';' or 'also', often with a quoted '<word> town/house/...' compound. The answer is ONE word that fits every part ('shanty': pub slang, a shack, shanty town). If the passages are only search hits for the clue's words, solve it from your own vocabulary. Never answer with a word from the clue itself ('poor') or with a page's category label.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - '<Category label> <Title>' with no 'this' ('Rock group Achtung Babies'): the label names the TYPE of the answer and the title is an anchor. If the passages show that the title is a near-copy of another work's name (a tribute or cover band, parody, namesake), answer with the ORIGINAL creator the passages tie it to ('U2'), not the tribute act, the album or a descriptor ('U2 tribute band').

edits.target: - A word in quotation marks inside the clue (a 'drag', a nickname) is usually a pun or hint tied to the answer. Look for passages where that word appears next to a candidate and answer with that candidate.
edits.content:
- When the quoted word is itself a generic head noun right after 'this' ('Fog forms when air cools to this "point"', 'this "bubble"'), it is the head of a standard compound that the passages repeat ('dew point'). Answer with the full compound, keeping the quoted word. Do not strip it to the bare modifier ('dew'). This is the head-noun exception to the delete-clue-words test, not an echo error.
- Short descriptor-plus-quote clues ('A comedienne: "Ball of Fire"') ask for the person, work or thing that the quoted phrase points to. The phrase may contain the answer's own name ('Ball' -> 'Lucille Ball') or be her known nickname. Pick the candidate whose name or alias is inside the phrase AND who fits the descriptor. A film or work that merely shares the title (such as a different actress who starred in Ball of Fire) is not the answer. Never answer with the quoted phrase itself. This works even when an archive snippet stops right after the clue.
- Grammar-role clues ('The adverb in "think fast"', 'the verb in ...', 'the noun in ...') are the one case where the answer IS a word from the clue (an explicit exception to the echo guard). Pick the single word inside the quoted phrase that has the named part of speech ('fast'), not a synonym ('quickly') and not the whole phrase. Passages that discuss the phrase (dictionary, grammar-forum or quiz-archive pages) confirm which word.

edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content: - Part-of-name clues ('First name of the man elected chancellor of a reunified Germany in 1990', 'Last name of...', 'Surname of...', 'Initials of...'): first identify the person from the passages (Helmut Kohl), then output ONLY the requested part ('Helmut'). Do not give the full name, a title, or a group label.
